learning: Iteration 9 to 10 showed that kd 0.8 to 1.0 moved slalom progress from 0.331 to 0.545, and that kp and ki had already flattened. The untested wheel_track 0.10 m lever was deliberately not used, because it cannot be checked before the final race.
notes: Final-iteration package: the Builder's iteration-10 geometry with the iteration-10 controller, unchanged. This is the best-scoring design (703.4) and the one carried to the unseen-track evaluation.
rationale:
This is the final iteration, so this package is the design carried into the unseen-track evaluation, and it must be the most reliable controller I have. Iteration 10 (kp 2.8, ki 0.7, kd 1.0, base_speed 1.3, last_direction) is the best race so far at 703.4. Oval and s-bend both complete 20 of 20. The slalom still fails 0 of 20, with progress 0.545 and max_error 0.0629 m, the best slalom progress yet. Iteration 9 to 10 changed only kd, from 0.8 to 1.0, and the score rose by 28.5. Earlier gains were flattening (ki 0.4 to 0.7 and kp 2.4 to 2.8 each moved the slalom only a little), and the kd step is the one that produced the new slalom progress.

The Builder's geometry for this iteration is identical to iteration 10: five sensors at y = 0.07 m, x = ±0.024 m, 12 mm footprint, 0.12 m track, 0.03 m wheels, 0.16 by 0.14 m body, 0.6 kg. I checked the Builder's intent against the evidence. Holding the geometry is the right call for a final, unrepeatable race. The wheel_track 0.10 m step is untested and would change turn rate on the oval and s-bend, where completion is currently 20 of 20. Line losses stay near 1 per run, far below the 2-per-run spread trigger, so no spread change is justified.

I therefore keep the iteration-10 controller exactly, rather than adding an untested gain change. Any change now would be unverifiable before the unseen-track race, and the proven controller is the safest choice. I expect oval and s-bend to hold at 20 of 20 and the slalom to show progress similar to iteration 10. I state no measured outcome for this package.
